The $\text{}^4\text{E}_g$ and $\text{}^4\text{A}_{1g}$ come from $\text{}^4\text{G}$.
So $E(\text{}^4\text{E}) \approx 10B + \dots$
If $E(\text{}^4\text{E}) = 23,000$, then $B$ should be around $2,300$. No, that's too high.
Wait, the free ion $\text{}^4\text{G}$ is $10B$.

$E/B = 45.648$.
So $E = 45.648 \times 540 = 24,650$.
If we want $E = 23,000$, then $B = 23,000 / 45.648 = 503.8$.
